expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: `export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription;` with each variant having `status: "trialing"` etc.

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: TrialingSubscription has only trialEndDate; CanceledSubscription has only canceledAt/cancelReason/voluntary — no shared optional fields.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Only mentions exhaustiveness prose-wise ("Switch statements force you to handle all cases"); no assertNever function or never-typed default arm is written.

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: `id: string; customerId: string; planId: string;` — bare strings, no branding.

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function; only "Want me to implement the state transition functions once you decide on those rules?"

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "**Impossible states prevented**: Can't have `cancelReason` on active subs (compile error)"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is a discriminated union with no optional fields; no single interface with `trialEndDate?` etc.
